title: H. G. Wells: The War of the Worlds — Ep 26/27 — "Wreckage"
description:
He remembers it all clearly, up to the moment he stood weeping and praising God on Primrose Hill — then nothing. Others find the dead Martians before he does, and the news flies to Paris while all England rings its bells; strangers hail him as the Last Man Left Alive and shelter him, gently breaking the news that Leatherhead is gone, every soul in it.

After four days the craving to see his home wins, and he leaves his hosts in tears for a free train through the wreckage. Past the terminus every house is a blackened shell, and every stream lies choked with red weed. The line is broken before Woking, so he walks on from Byfleet toward Maybury, passing the warped, broken dog cart and the horse's gnawed white bones in the weed.

At his house the door has been forced. Upstairs his unfinished paper still lies on the desk, broken mid-sentence, and the mutton rots on the table below — his home desolate. A voice says no one escaped but him. He turns, and on the step, amazed and afraid as he is, stand his cousin and his wife.

She is white and tearless, and when he steps toward her she gives a faint cry before he can believe it. Swaying on the threshold, one hand at her throat, she tells him: "I came. I knew... I knew..." — and he catches her in his arms.

Chapter IX of Book Two of H. G. Wells's The War of the Worlds (1898), "Wreckage", in the public domain.

— The Keeper's Lantern —
Every episode is one whole chapter, in order, from the first page to the last.
